audit.whatIsWrong: Level 1 and Levels 4-5 were 'Skill' while their own whys said the levels were Warwick's, and the first-item and 2-item rows were given to Warwick while whys[5] and whys[6] both said Vladimir takes over. whys[1] said 'Level 2 is even' on a row already marked Warwick.
audit.why: Transfusion costs Vladimir health rather than mana and his early damage is low, so Warwick's Q heal-for-damage-dealt wins every short trade until Vladimir has health and haste; after his first item Transfusion falls to 4.6s and out-sustains the chip.
audit.corrected: Rows 0 and 3 to Warwick, rows 5 and 6 to Vladimir, as matched full/content pairs with ratings moved to match, and whys[1] rewritten so Level 2 no longer reads as even.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[5].why sold Blade of the Ruined King as the deciding first-item spike on a row that belongs to Vladimir.
audit.why: Vladimir's health-and-haste item is the bigger spike: Transfusion goes from 9s at rank 1 to 4.6s at rank 5, and Crimson Pact converts each 30 bonus health into ability power, so his item purchases feed both bars at once.
audit.corrected: phases[5].why re-keyed to Transfusion's 4.6s cooldown; phases[6].why re-keyed to Hemoplague's damage amp and per-champion heal.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1].text and mid both claimed Sanguine Pool 'untargets him mid-channel' / 'mid-Infinite-Duress', which asserts that a suppressed Vladimir can still cast Pool. Riot's text does not say that. Separately, Tides of Blood being blocked by units was never mentioned anywhere.
audit.why: Riot's own description of Tides of Blood says it 'can be blocked by enemy units', so standing behind your own minions is a free damage reduction against his main poke. Sanguine Pool is 28/25/22/19/16s for 2 seconds of untargetability; Infinite Duress is a 1.5s suppression on 110/90/70. Whether Pool can be cast while suppressed is not in the data, so the advice is stated pre-emptively — spend your R only once Pool is gone — which is correct either way.
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text and mid rewritten to the pre-emptive framing with the real 1.5s / 110s / 2s numbers; dosFull[1].d now states the minion-block on Tides of Blood; dontsFull[0].d carries Pool's 28s rank-1 cooldown; dontsFull[1].d states Crimson Pact turning bonus health into AP, which is why 'Stack pure HP' is the wrong answer to him.

audit.why: Mercury's Treads and early Executioner's Calling are already listed, which is the right answer to a health-costed sustain champion.

edits.before: Level 2 is even before either champ has a committal trade pattern online.
edits.after: Level 2 is yours: Transfusion costs him health, and your Q heals what it deals.

edits.before: Blade of the Ruined King is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Sanguine Pool's cooldown.
edits.after: His health-and-haste item lands first: Transfusion drops to 4.6s and out-heals everything you chip in.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Vladimir carry threat 8.5/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Hemoplague amps what his team lands and heals him per champion hit — carry threat 8.5/10, so hunt his backline instead of duelling.

edits.before: That is Vladimir's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Sanguine Pool is 28s at rank 1 and 2s untargetable — make him spend it first.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Crimson Pact turns his bonus health into AP — buy magic resist.

edits.before: Q-bite Vladimir as he steps up (hold Q to follow his dash), weave autos, and let the passive out-heal his return damage.
edits.after: Stand behind your minions — Tides of Blood is blocked by units, so the wave eats his E while your Q bite heals you back up.

edits.before: Your Infinite Duress all-in is strong here, but Sanguine Pool untargets him mid-channel, so time R for the moment his W is down and Blood Hunt is active for the speed and heal.
edits.after: Infinite Duress is a 1.5s suppress on a 110s cooldown, so spend it only once Sanguine Pool is gone — two seconds of untargetability answers the leap if he pools before it connects.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are even as he starts stacking, and your level-6 all-in is real, but Pool untargets him mid-Infinite-Duress and wastes your ult if you mistime it. Commit R only when his W is down and Blood Hunt is up for the extra speed and lifesteal.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay yours while his health stacking is thin, and your level-6 all-in is real — but a two-second Pool spent before your leap connects burns the whole 110s ultimate. Commit R only once his W is gone and Blood Hunt is up for the speed.

notes: packet suspectName 'Your Infinite Duress' in spikes[1].text is a FALSE POSITIVE — Infinite Duress is Warwick's real R name. The real problem in that line was the mid-channel Pool claim, which I replaced with pre-emptive advice rather than reversing, matching what the mirror did. Tides of Blood being blocked by enemy units is stated in Riot's own description and appeared nowhere on the page; it is the most actionable early-lane fact here.
